text: This is FIRMHAND. A small company run by three agents, one shared ledger, and you.
Sales quotes customers. Operations moves stock. Finance posts every cent. Each has its own inbox, its own rules and its own permissions, and they only meet in the shared records.
On day two, a café asks for eighteen percent off. Sales may give ten. So the run stops, and the request waits for me, bound to its exact terms by a hash.

Day three. Grinder demand quadruples and the supplier slips. Nobody asks me. Operations sizes an expedite, Finance funds it inside budget, and Sales re-promises dates to the customers who are waiting.
Day five. Operations crashes mid-turn, and it does not announce it. Finance notices because work stopped moving, freezes spending, and asks me before anything restarts.
After the restart, Operations finishes its half-packed parcels exactly once, then catches up.
Every number opens the records behind it. Revenue is posted on dispatch, never on booking.
Any day replays from the event log alone, with no side effects. And against a naive company with the same seed, it keeps every customer.
FIRMHAND. One company. One shared truth.
